R0 tested gaussian3+jpeg4 (28.22) and gaussian4+jpeg3 (28.48) separately but never the joint lowering gaussian3+jpeg3; if the plateau is a symmetric severity overestimate this combination should converge.

R1 unexplained-signal boundary test: target variance_ratio=0.732 vs gaussian5+jpeg4 sim 0.887 (−0.155 shortfall) is the only signal not explained by blur+JPEG; R0 tested contrast_weaken_stretch:2 and contrast_weaken_scale:2 (both −4.8 to −7.1 dB) but never the mild sev1 boundary. If a weak contrast step is real, sev1 is the only unexplored point; if PSNR/CI still degrade, global is definitively a blur+JPEG byproduct.

The only untested corner of the plausible gaussian3-5 x jpeg3-4 grid is gaussian5+jpeg3; test it to confirm the ~28dB deterministic plateau and rule out a >2dB CHANGE (threshold >30.21dB).

alternatives: blur_glass:5,compression_jpeg:4 (PSNR 27.41, CI 8/10; glass DT branch still possible, glass_score shown to be JPEG-inflated)
final_decision.rationale: JPEG presence is certain (block_boundary=8.393, 0%FP; dct_zero_ratio=0.957). Strong blur certain (gm_ratio=0.199). Noise and global ruled out by peeled §B (sigma<2, structured residual) and by three global tests that each cost 4-7dB / CI collapse. Blur subtype: glass DT signal (glass_score=1.62) is contradicted by a control — pure gaussian:5+jpeg:4 simulation scores glass_score=1.69, proving JPEG inflates glass_score; gaussian family wins on wiener kernel self-consistency (MATCH vs glass 0.831) and PSNR (28.2 vs 27.4). Severity: sim analysis of gaussian5+jpeg4 (gm_ratio 0.138, spectral slope ratio 1.389) vs target (0.199, 1.132) shows gaussian5 is over-blurred → sev4 (sev3 ties at PSNR but is the boundary of the scan). JPEG sev4 preferred over 3 on the 0%FP block signal (CI 1% vs 16%) despite sev3 PSNR +0.27dB. No candidate exceeds 30dB — a plateau consistent with an unresolved stochastic component (glass shuffle cannot be excluded) or off-grid severity; verdict stays UNCERTAIN, training PSNR must arbitrate. Single support (k=1, pair0 only): final candidates were verified on the only support pair; cross-pair validation impossible.
